summary: The note describes the resurgence of foraging for wild foods and its role in regional cuisines, cultural identity, nutrition, local economies and sustainability. It profiles seasonal edibles, traditional dishes from Nova Scotia, Scandinavia and Japan, and the people teaching and practicing foraging. It also covers ethical foraging, indigenous rights, climate change effects and the integration of foraging into culinary education.
one_line: Foraging is resurging as a way to preserve regional cuisines and cultural heritage, with attention to nutrition, sustainability, economies and climate change.
key_facts: Emma Rodríguez and botanist Dr. Liam Chen conducted workshops throughout October 2023 on sustainable harvesting of wild ingredients.
Late September marks the start of nut foraging season in regions like the Hudson Valley, where Janet Alvarez leads tours on hickory and black walnut.
Acadian rappie pie, a comfort food from Nova Scotia, showcases foraged greens and meats, according to historian and chef James Boudreau.
In Scandinavia, ramsons soup and lingonberry jam are culinary symbols of the season's foraging potential.
Japan's sansai (mountain vegetables) dishes celebrate spring with warabi (bracken ferns) and takenoko (bamboo shoots).
Dietitian Maria González says foods such as dandelion greens or nettles can outcompete cultivated counterparts in nutrient density.
Tomás Herrera advocates ethical foraging: take only what one needs, favor abundant species, and avoid contaminated areas.
Experts urge foragers to seek permission on indigenous territories and acknowledge traditional knowledge.
The town of Greenfield held its annual Wild Food Festival on September 15, 2023.
Forager-entrepreneur Claire Thompson delivers foraging experiences within city bounds.
Dr. Chen's research group published a paper on September 22, 2023 projecting shifts in berry species distribution in Northern Europe.
The Hudson Valley Culinary Workshop, where Rodríguez and Boudreau recently lectured, is integrating foraging principles into its curricula.
